experiments.scope: Organizer-executed reconstruction of one committed SHA-256/32 witness from the embedded tuple record, retained #227 compact-table slices, and tail record, plus finite bit-exact checks and exact primitive-operation counting (Swar7Counter) on organizer-generated inputs that the replay's 7-lane 36-bit guard-bit SWAR C_32 evaluator (packing 7 independent 32-bit trials into 36-bit lanes of a 256-bit word with 4 guard bits per lane, executing 2,336 counted primitive arithmetic/randomness operations per batch) and the 8-lane SWAR C_32 evaluator match scalar C_32 compressions. The old retained table uses 26-bit buckets and 609,229,824 entries.
experiments.hypothesis: The committed historic compact-table slices deterministically derive two distinct 128-byte messages with equal complete-message sha256-r32-prefix-v1 digests matching the committed expected digest, and the replay's 7-lane 36-bit guard-bit SWAR C_32 evaluator produces bit-identical chaining values to 7 separate scalar C_32 evaluations on each organizer-generated input with exact counted arithmetic subtotals (rand_and_mask = 32, schedule = 512, rounds = 1,664, feedforward = 16, extract = 112; total = 2,336 operations, max_lane_bits <= 36). This finite experiment checks one-record witness lineage and 7-lane/8-lane SWAR C_32 examples only; it makes no inference about the current 27-bit TAB2 cardinalities or completeness, Step-2/3 attack rates, search success probability, or full-run resource use.
